name: Jetson AGX Thor Developer Kit

sources.title: NVIDIA Jetson Thor page ("Jetson Thor Series" technical specifications table: Jetson AGX Thor Developer Kit, Jetson T5000, Jetson T4000)
sources.covers: camera, PCIe, USB, networking, power and mechanical rows (the T5000 and T4000 share the camera, PCIe and USB cells)

note: Camera: "HSB camera via QSFP slot | USB camera" (the kit has no MIPI CSI-2 camera connector in the table, so lanes is null; HSB is NVIDIA's Holoscan Sensor Bridge, over the QSFP28 port). USB: "2x USB-A (3.2 Gen2) | 2x USB-C (3.1)" (ports 2 and stated_mbps 10000 are the USB-A 3.2 Gen 2 ports, the USB-IF per-port signalling rate; the USB-C ports' generation is not stated). PCIe: "M.2 Key M slot with x4 PCIe Gen5 | M.2 Key E slot with x1 PCIe Gen5". Networking: "1x 5GbE RJ45 connector | 1x QSFP28 (4x 25GbE)". Power "40 W–130 W" (power_w 130, the upper end). Mechanical "243.19 mm x 112.40 mm x 56.88 mm" (size_mm as stated, not an optical frame); mass not stated. The module is a Jetson T5000 (the page's kit table). The page's footnotes: "* Refer to the Software Features section of the latest NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide for a list of supported features. ** Low-speed I/O specification is subject to change." The module data sheet was not read; the figures are the specifications table on the page. practical_mbps is null (not stated).
interface: USB 3.2 Gen 2 (USB-A), USB 3.1 (USB-C, generation not stated), QSFP28 (4x 25GbE, Holoscan Sensor Bridge), PCIe Gen5
